body:
I can’t reproduce this, the following valid test case works fine:

``` js
{ code: "(function () {\n  /* foo */\n  console.log('bla');\n  /* bar */\n})", args: [1, "never"]}
```
Can you paste in what you see on the console with that example?

Of course:

```
app.js
  26:32  error  Block must not be padded by blank lines  padded-blocks
```

Line 26 is the line that contains the first comment:

```
/*eslint-disable consistent-return*/
```
It seems like this is an esprima bug. The comments are not attached to the  `ReturnStatement`. If you replace the `ReturnStatement` with anything else (a function call for instance) it works.
Weird. Can you for an esprima bug?

Good news! We're going to be using our own parser starting with the next minor release. I've opened an Espree bug for this: https://github.com/eslint/espree/issues/2

Hopefully we can figure out a way to fix it ourselves and move on.
Update: just created a fix in Espree: https://github.com/eslint/espree/pull/18

body: This bug has been fixed. That said, decorators are not supported by the default parser of eslint, so I guess you are using a different parser, please file an issue there.
I use eslint 0.23, should I install customer parser for it? Which one?
If you use the default parser you should get a syntax error for any decorator. I think the only parser that supports decorators is `babel-eslint`.
Oh, sorry. I already use it. But the issue is still actual.
Then this is a bug in `babel-eslint`.
